desc:
The leaf sequence of a binary tree is the list of the values of its leaves (nodes without any child), read from left to right. Two trees can look very different and still have the same leaf sequence.

Given two binary trees a and b, return true if their leaf sequences are equal and false otherwise. The empty tree has an empty leaf sequence.

How trees are given. There is no tree type here. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level-order (top to bottom, left to right), the same way LeetCode serialises trees. A missing child is written as -1, and every real node value is non-negative. The children of a missing node are not listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped, so a non-empty array never ends with -1. The empty tree is [].

For example, [1, 2, 3, -1, 4] describes the tree on the left: the root is 1 with children 2 and 3, node 2 has no left child and has 4 as its right child, and node 3 is a leaf.

    1
   / \
  2   3
   \
    4

Both arguments use this encoding. For a = [1, 2, 3] and b = [5, 8, -1, 2, 3] both leaf sequences are [2, 3], so the answer is true. For a = [1, 2, 3] and b = [1, 3, 2] the sequences are [2, 3] and [3, 2], so the answer is false.
constraints: 0 ≤ number of nodes in each tree ≤ 1,500
Both arrays follow the encoding above exactly (valid level-order, no trailing -1)
hints: A leaf is a node with no left child and no right child. Be careful: a node with one child is not a leaf.
Leaves are met in left-to-right order when you traverse the tree in preorder (or inorder), always going left before right.
Collect the leaf sequence of each tree with an iterative preorder (stack: push right, then left) and compare the two lists.
editorial: Any depth-first traversal that always visits the left subtree before the right one meets the leaves in left-to-right order, so collect the leaves of each tree during such a traversal and compare the two lists for equality. A node is a leaf exactly when it has neither child; a node with a single child must not be recorded.

Both traversals are linear. If the trees are huge and the sequences differ early you could stop sooner by advancing the two traversals in lock-step, one leaf at a time, and returning false at the first mismatch; the worst case stays O(n + m), and this version uses only the stack space of the two traversals instead of storing complete leaf lists.
